reply.thought: The batch is now with me. I need to retrieve each customer's net balance (order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance and then record a payout for each customer.

I need the customer identifier to query net_balance. The batch information from Alpha Co was not provided, so I cannot proceed. I will request the list of orders (or the customer details) needed to compute each customer’s net balance.

Now that I have the list of orders with customers and amounts, I can compute each customer’s net balance (order amounts minus refunds) using net_balance. I need to call net_balance for each distinct customer: acme, birch, and cobalt.
I have the net balance for customer acme (29477 cents). Next, I need the net balance for customer birch.
I have the net balance for customer birch (20191 cents). Next, I need the net balance for customer cobalt.
I now have the net balances for all customers: acme 29477 cents, birch 20191 cents, cobalt 12494 cents. I need to record a payout for each customer using record_payout.

result.error: bad arguments: World.record_payout() got an unexpected keyword argument 'amount_cent'. Did you mean 'amount_cents'?

reply.thought: The record_payout call failed because the argument name is 'amount_cents', not 'amount_cent'. I will correct the argument name and resend the record_payout request for customer acme.
The payout for customer acme has been recorded successfully. Next, I need to record the payout for customer birch.
The payout for customer birch has been recorded successfully. Next, I need to record the payout for customer cobalt.
The previous tool call failed because the name was incorrectly written as 'record_ payout' with an extra space. I need to call the correct tool 'record_payout' for customer cobalt.
All three payouts have been recorded successfully. The batch is complete.
